title: Typed layer features
description: What the typed layer adds on top of the JSON layer's behaviour; month ends, gaps and overlaps, exact arithmetic and ranges are the JSON layer's features, which the typed operations call.

entities.name: Valid by construction
entities.description: A typed value that exists is a value that can exist: constructors refuse 30 February, hour 25 or a reversed interval.
entities.behavior: The civil constructors (of, of_hms, of_hms_nano, at_offset) build the value's UTV JSON and read it back with the JSON layer's reader, so the same checks apply as for incoming JSON; Interval::of checks its points and order, and of_ratio its denominator, directly. A refusal is Err(Diagnostics) with the shared code (day-out-of-range, month-out-of-range, field-out-of-range, leap-second, offset-out-of-range, reversed-interval, unsupported-form, implementation-limit), and Diagnostics implements std::error::Error, so ? works.
entities.outcome: Code that holds a CivilDate never has to ask whether it is a real date, and a bad input is reported with the reason, never a panic.
constraints: Rust has no exceptions, so of returns Result<T, Diagnostics>; there is no separate try_of.
Constructors also refuse a year whose day numbers leave i128 (implementation-limit), so later total operations can compute with it.

entities.name: Total operations return values, partial ones an Outcome
entities.description: Only an operation that time can refuse to answer returns an Outcome, so every Outcome in user code marks such a question.
entities.behavior: Total operations (add_days, add_months_constrained, days_until, Instant::add, Interval::contains) return the value itself. Partial ones (add_months, add, resolve, compare, parse, from_json) return Outcome<T>: Unique(T, Diagnostics), Multiple(Vec<T>, Diagnostics) ascending, None, Unsupported or Invalid, each with its diagnostics. Helpers never pick an answer: unique() and unique_or() take only Unique, single() turns anything else into an OutcomeError carrying the status and codes, and Display prints none (month-end).
entities.outcome: A developer matches on the cases that can happen and cannot silently get one of two DST instants.
constraints: A JSON-layer status other than none and invalid (symbolic, error, ...) becomes Unsupported.
A total operation panics if the JSON layer refuses anyway, which for valid values means arithmetic beyond i128, the way integer overflow panics in Rust.
Never use Outcome::*: its None would shadow Option::None.

entities.name: Typed policies
entities.description: Month-end, gap and overlap policies are enums, and the policy that can't fail has its own method.
entities.behavior: MonthEnd { Reject, Constrain }, Gap { Reject, PreserveUnresolved, ShiftForward }, Overlap { Reject, All, Earliest, Latest } and ResolutionPolicy (STRICT, the default; ALL_CANDIDATES; new(gap, overlap)) are written into the JSON layer's policy objects. The clamping month arithmetic is a separate total method (add_months_constrained, add_years_constrained); add_months and add_years reject, and add_with(period, month_end) takes either policy.
entities.outcome: A policy is checked by the compiler, and MonthEnd::Reject can never reach a method that has to return a plain value.
constraints: Rust has no overloads, so the total forms are separate methods rather than add_months(n, MonthEnd::Constrain).
Every policy value the enums allow is implemented, so unsupported-policy can't arise from the typed layer.

entities.name: Order only where the rules can't change it
entities.description: Values compare with < only when their order doesn't depend on zone rules; zoned values compare through the context.
entities.behavior: CivilDate, CivilYearMonth, CivilTime, CivilDateTime, FixedOffsetDateTime (by instant, then offset, then wall time) and Instant (exactly) implement Ord. A missing second counts as 0, then 09:30 comes before 09:30:00, so that Ord agrees with Eq. ZonedIntent has no Ord: TemporalContext::compare resolves both strictly and answers Outcome<Ordering>, Multiple when the order depends on an overlap.
entities.outcome: No comparison operator can return an order that a change of zone rules would make false.
constraints: Equality is representation: 09:30 and 09:30:00 are different values.
compare refuses with the resolution's own outcome (gap, unknown-zone, outside-rule-window, offset-mismatch).

entities.name: Values print as their text form
entities.description: Display is the UTV text form, Debug names the type, and exact second counts print as display strings.
entities.behavior: Display on a typed value is format_text of its JSON (2026-11-05, P1M, [2026-11-01, ..)); where the text form can't express the value losslessly it prints the JSON instead. Debug is CivilDate(2026-11-05). PosixSeconds and ElapsedSeconds have no text form and print 3600.75 s (POSIX), 1/3 s (POSIX) or 86400 s (SI). parse and FromStr read the text form back.
entities.outcome: A value can be logged and read back without loss, and a second count can't be mistaken for a parseable value.
constraints: PosixSeconds and ElapsedSeconds have no parse or FromStr.
An Instant with a fraction that has no finite decimal (1/3 s) has no text form and prints as JSON.

entities.name: Zone rules held in an explicit context
entities.description: Zoned operations take a TemporalContext built from rules the caller loaded; there is no global or default one.
entities.behavior: TemporalContext::with(ZoneRules::load(path)?) holds one rule bundle. resolve, resolve_with, in_zone and compare use only those rules; ZonedIntent::resolve(&ctx) and Instant::in_zone(id, &ctx) are the same operations.
entities.outcome: Which rules produced an answer is visible in the code that asked, and nothing reads the host's tz database.
constraints: ZoneRules is the JSON layer's Rules; zones it doesn't list and times outside its window are unsupported.
